summary: I counted the headings before reading the entry's claim: exactly two `## D-089`, and the only duplicate among seventy-six, with D-080 through D-088 each appearing once. The blocks are not copies — 1959 bytes against 1894, neither a superset — so a plain deletion with no union clause had to be earned rather than assumed. I probed every substantive claim unique to the block being deleted and block 1 carries all eight, which is why D-087 needed a union and this does not. The keep choice is not merely defensible but necessary: block 1 uniquely holds the one-sentence-summary edit and the refusal to mark DR-103/118/119/123 SATISFIED, and block 2 holds neither. The stated cause verifies too, further than I could take it at D-087 — the first commit wrote COORD and file 08, the second wrote COORD only, so the register was written exactly once and the duplication is confined to the decision log.
whatIVerified: Subject digest at start and end: b240d5e9fd191b4a150ee2107e666aa1138fe80d4a1299eeae3ff5e9627071a4, three measurements each, equal to the dispatched value, -r--r--r-- at both ends. Prompt held at c2a58b01… across start and end.

The attack 'heading count is not actually two' fails, and I established the count independently before reading the subject's Fact section so as not to be anchored by it. `## D-089 — Record DR-115 SATISFIED under D-056 Class B` appears at lines 3545 and 3585, twice. A frequency sweep across all seventy-six `## D-nnn` headings returns D-089 as the sole duplicated id, and a targeted census of the D-08x range confirms D-080 through D-088 each appear exactly once against ten adopted commits, so there is no second recording defect hiding behind this one.

The two recitals are not duplicates in the ordinary sense, which is the fact that makes a plain deletion non-trivial and which I tested before accepting it. Block 1 is 1959 bytes and block 2 is 1894, and a line diff shows each carries wording the other lacks. Their heads are identical — both record ADOPTED 2026-08-14, turn 2 of 3, CONSENT from both reviewers at 0 MUST-FIX and 0 SHOULD-FIX, and both cite the same frozen turn-2 subject a31cf8ee… and the same two verdict digests.

The decisive question for a deletion with no union clause is whether anything substantive is unique to the block being removed, and nothing is. I extracted every substantive claim appearing only in block 2 and probed block 1 for each: the turn-1 Codex advisory IDs, the refusal to overturn D-088, the unique lead-prefix replacement, DR-115's named measurement remainder, the preservation of D-085's remainders, DR-103's contract note, the 2-of-30 count and the NOT MET standing. Block 1 covers all eight. Block 2's wording is in places tidier — it writes 'Turn-1 Codex' and spells ADV-D089-01 / 02 / 03 in full, and it carries 'Does not overturn D-088' in the Decision-type line rather than only in Reversibility — but no claim is lost by removing it. This is the point at which D-087 required a union sentence and this entry does not, and I checked rather than assumed the difference.

The keep choice is stronger than the entry's own rationale states. Block 1 uniquely holds two operative items that block 2 omits entirely: 'Replace only "condition 2 remains 1 of 30 SATISFIED" in the one-sentence summary', which is the fourth of D-089's file-08 edits, and 'Do not mark DR-103/118/119/123 SATISFIED', the refusal that my own turn-1 MUST-FIX on D-089 turned on. Keeping the first is therefore necessary, not merely preferable, and the stated rejection 'Delete the first and keep the second. Rejected: the first already names the non-SATISFIED of DR-103/118/119/123' is accurate as far as it goes.

The block-1 identifier verifies at byte level. The entry names it as 'the block that begins immediately after C-D085', and the bytes immediately preceding its heading are 'Overturn: C-D085.
- **Commit:** C-D085.

---

', with D-085 the nearest preceding heading. There is no ambiguity about which block is kept.

The deletion boundary in clause 2 matches the file's structure. Block 2's heading is preceded by '
---

', so 'from the horizontal rule that precedes its heading' names a real rule, and block 2's final line is '- **Commit:** C-D089.'. Block 2 is the last content in the file, so after the deletion COORD ends at block 1's own Commit line with no orphaned rule.

The stated cause verifies, and I was able to test the mechanism here rather than only the effect as at D-087. At the D-085 commit COORD carried zero `## D-089` headings. Commit acdfaed added one, and changed file 08 from 18713a60… to 36ecbea8…, so that is the commit that performed the MF-6 write. Commit 7aee1e5 added the second heading, touched COORD only at +40 lines, and left file 08 unchanged at 36ecbea8…. So 'two apply writers appended in the same commit window' is exactly right, and the important negative result is that the register was written once: a duplicated recital did not come with a duplicated file-08 write.

D-089's write itself applied correctly, which matters because the duplication could have masked a bad write. The string 'SATISFIED 2026-08-14 (D-089 / D-056 Class B)' occurs exactly once in file 08, and `**DECIDED-V1-NOT-INTEGRATED**` now occurs four times where it occurred five. That is direct evidence in bytes that the unique-prefix repair my turn-1 D089-MF-1 required did what it was meant to: one row flipped, and DR-104, DR-118, DR-119 and DR-123 were left alone.

The attack 'changes D-089 substance' fails. The header states 'Does not amend D-089's adopted substance', the readiness effect is 'Zero. D-089's readiness effect is unchanged', clause 3 refuses to reopen D-089 or edit its frozen subjects and verdicts, and the only content motion is the removal of a block whose every claim survives in the block that stays.

The entry's factual assertions about the current register are true: file 08 records DR-115's lead as '**SATISFIED 2026-08-14 (D-089 / D-056 Class B).**', its Blueprint impact as 'Architecture-preview SATISFIED under D-056 Class B (D-089). Measurement remains condition 4 / DR-G01..G05 / DR-012 qualification…', and condition 2 as '2 of 30 `SATISFIED`' with standing NOT MET.

The attacks 'silent SATISFIED', 'file 08 edited' and 'condition 5 / docs/v2/implementation' all fail on a line-by-line audit. Every SATISFIED occurrence in the subject is a refusal, a quotation of the D-089 heading, a description of what file 08 already records, or the unchanged 2-of-30 standing; the header and clause 3 each refuse file-08 edits and the implementation directory; the readiness effect keeps condition 5 last. file 08 measures 36ecbea8…, matching the pin, and git reports both it and COORD unmodified in my working tree.

All three measured inputs match live bytes — COORD 92186f05…, file 08 36ecbea8… and the freeze e809d439… — and both D-089 commits resolve at full hash to identically titled commits, which is itself consistent with the two-writer account. Both recital verdict digests also verify: my own D-089 turn-2 verdict at e920fa6a… and the Codex one at a2291f07…, the latter hashed without opening.

The form citation holds: D-087 and D-080 are both present in COORD and are recital-correction entries of the same class, and D-087 in particular is the direct precedent — the entry cites it again in rejecting a silent working-tree edit. D-090 is absent from COORD, so adoption creates no collision.
Reversibility matches the act: one deletion, one restoration, 'C-D090 plus restore of the deleted second recital.'
I wrote one file, the verdict named for me, and edited and committed nothing.

consentNote: I CONSENT with zero MUST-FIX and zero SHOULD-FIX. The trap in a de-duplication entry is that the two blocks are not actually duplicates, and here they are not — 1959 bytes against 1894, with wording unique to each. What separates this from D-087, where I required the union clause to be present, is that there I found substantive content only in the block marked for deletion, and here I found none: I probed block 1 for all eight claims that appear only in block 2 and it carries every one. The keep choice also turns out to be necessary rather than merely reasonable, since block 1 alone holds the one-sentence-summary edit and the DR-103/118/119/123 refusal. The part I could not do at D-087 I could do here — the commit walk shows the first writer touched COORD and file 08 and the second touched COORD alone, so the register was written exactly once, and file 08 confirms it: one SATISFIED lead written, and the four other DECIDED rows still standing at four.
